notes.title: A Comic Love Story: LKY, Summer Case Files, and a Little Girl
notes.notes:
[p]LKY loved comics.
Back in the 90s, in his hometown, there were roadside book stalls—simple setups tucked into alleyways: two or three shelves, five or six tiny stools. Novels cost 3.5 cents per volume, while comics were just 1.5 cents. You couldn’t borrow them; you could only read on-site. With limited stools but plenty of readers, LKY often squatted against a wall, absorbed in reading for entire afternoons.[/p][p]Back then, LKY’s favorite manga artists were Akira Toriyama, Masami Kurumada, Rumiko Takahashi, and Tsukasa Hojo. If he had to pick just one, it would be Rumiko Takahashi. Not because of Ranma ½ or Urusei Yatsura, but because of Koisuru Kisetsu—also known as Maison Ikkoku. At the time, Inuyasha hadn’t even been released yet. Even after Inuyasha became a phenomenon later on, Koisuru Kisetsu remained LKY’s all-time favorite manga.[/p][p]He remembered he’d been chasing after Peacock King by Shungicu Uejima, but it was so popular that every time he went to the stall, someone else had already grabbed it. Since Ranma ½ was great, LKY picked up Koisuru Kisetsu from a pile of shoujo manga—and fell head over heels.[/p][p]Well, there was a little side story to that “falling head over heels,” but rest assured, it was absolutely because Koisuru Kisetsu was so good, not because she was so pretty.[/p][p]It was a summer evening. LKY, back then just a third- or fourth-grader, was reading Koisuru Kisetsu. He couldn’t remember which volume anymore—only that the story was getting really good. His backpack was cushioning his bottom as he leaned against the wall, completely absorbed. After a while, he caught a whiff of peaches. A little girl with a ponytail had squatted down beside him, intently reading the same manga in his hands—Koisuru Kisetsu. LKY froze. The page he’d been about to turn stopped mid-flip. When the next page didn’t come, the girl looked up. Their eyes met.
Boom.
Something exploded in LKY’s mind. He quickly lowered his head, pretending nothing had happened, and resumed reading Koisuru Kisetsu. He flipped a page, waited a bit—long enough to pretend he was reading—then flipped another. That evening, LKY finished two volumes of Koisuru Kisetsu, but he couldn’t recall a single thing he’d read.[/p][p]Borrowing books was common. With limited pocket money and endless books to read, LKY often shared with friends—today I borrow yours, tomorrow you borrow mine. LKY was a bit stingy—if a friend kept borrowing without returning the favor, he’d get annoyed. But that little girl never let him borrow anything, and yet, LKY never got mad. Not only that, he began to secretly hope she’d come to read with him. If she didn’t show up one day, he’d feel lost, and reading just wasn’t as enjoyable. So from then on, whenever LKY arrived at the stall, he’d first scan the area to see if she was there. If she wasn’t, he’d read something else first. As for Koisuru Kisetsu? He’d just wait. Such a wonderful story shouldn’t be read half-heartedly or without flavor.[/p][p]In the 90s, there were many roadside stalls—simple wooden pushcarts with only two wheels, pulled or pushed by hand. Villagers loaded them with produce and hauled them into town early each morning to sell. The little girl helped her family sell peaches from one such cart. She only came to read when most of the peaches were sold. Sometimes, if the peaches didn’t sell out even by nightfall, Koisuru Kisetsu would remain unread all day.[/p][p]Having the book right there but resisting the urge to read it—doable for a day or two, but impossible over time. After a few days of restless struggle, LKY finally gave in to the temptation of Koisuru Kisetsu. Even today, the feeling of opening it alone remains vivid—a sense of guilty infidelity. Reading it by himself felt like betraying the little girl who used to share it with him. Yet when he waited for her to arrive, it felt like he was abandoning Koisuru Kisetsu itself—as if Kyoko, the heroine, was already scolding him for being a heartless man.[/p][p]Still, LKY had his tricks. Every time he borrowed Koisuru Kisetsu, he’d take several extra volumes—ones that came right after where the girl had last read. Just enough, never too many, so they’d last until the stall closed at dusk. Of course, LKY had already read those volumes himself—he was far ahead in the story—but no matter how far he got, he always remembered the last volume they’d read together. From then on, LKY developed a new skill: reading while staying alert to his surroundings. The moment the girl appeared at the alley’s entrance, he’d sense it instantly. He’d close the volume he was actually reading, pick up one of the “extra” ones, and slowly, deliberately, pretend to just be starting.[/p][p]That summer, LKY insisted on bringing his own money for breakfast, yet went hungry every morning. That summer, he watched his friends lick ice pops, his mouth watering, but never bought one himself. That same summer, starving and lightheaded, he never bought a single pack of Little Raccoon crackers. All for the comics. Because Koisuru Kisetsu was just too good—and he needed to read it twice. Though each comic cost only 1.5 cents, Koisuru Kisetsu had dozens of volumes. Every penny he’d saved up went straight into that alleyway stall. That summer, LKY truly understood the saying: “Love makes even water taste like a feast.”[/p][p]It must have been August, halfway through summer break. LKY can’t remember how many volumes of Koisuru Kisetsu they’d read together, only that the story had reached the part where Godai proposed to Kyoko—near the end. LKY had matured a bit, or perhaps didn’t want it to end, so he no longer rushed through the final volumes. By then, he’d started reading Cat’s Eye—those long legs were utterly mesmerizing. But his heart still belonged to Koisuru Kisetsu. He only used those alluring figures to distract himself. It was a kind of waiting—a desire to savor the sweetest ending with his dearest companion.[/p][p]But then, one day, the cart piled with peaches disappeared. The girl who used to borrow books never came back. At first, LKY didn’t mind, still entranced by the black catsuits in Cat’s Eye. One day passed, then two, three, a week, half a month. Summer break was ending. School was about to start. The girl still hadn’t appeared. Suddenly, those long legs weren’t appealing anymore. The tight outfits held no charm. LKY panicked. Cat’s Eye couldn’t distract him now. He kept running to the alley’s entrance, only to return disappointed. He searched the streets a few times, wondering if her family had moved to a different selling spot—but found nothing.[/p][p]One midday at the end of August, LKY trudged home, crestfallen. His mom was busy cooking lunch. She said there was fruit on the table if he was hungry. LKY slumped over the dining table, chin resting on his hand, staring blankly at the plastic fruit bowl in the center. One, two, three, four—four nectarines, familiar yet strange. He sniffed, lowered his head, and wiped his eyes on the back of his hand. His mom, chopping vegetables, casually mentioned, “Peach season’s almost over. Eat these today—there won’t be any more after.” Obediently, LKY picked up one nectarine and took a small bite. The soft, juicy fruit was sweet, with a hint of tartness—and just a touch of salt.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]Summer Case Files has been out for nearly a month now. It’s time to write something down as a keepsake. Of course, the main goal is also to boost visibility—maybe even flip this underdog onto its winning side. This is a true childhood story from LKY’s life, shared in hopes of bringing you a smile.[/p][p]If you enjoyed this little tale, you might also like Summer Case Files. If you’re willing, please give it a try.
And if you’ve already supported Summer Case Files,
we’d be endlessly grateful if you could use your lucky hands to give it a thumbs-up and leave a review on STEAM. Thank you from the bottom of our hearts.[/p]

notes.title: "Gratitude in Heart, Yet Ashamed to Accept It" - Delay Announcement
notes.notes:
Opening Ramble:

For LKY, anxiety has become the norm.

Every time LKY needs to announce a delay, sleepless nights follow. Even if LKY manages to fall asleep at two or three in the morning, waking up at 5:30 AM is inevitable. Feeling extremely tired but unable to get back to sleep.

Each delay announcement requires LKY to build up psychological strength for a long time, from initially one day to now three or four days.

The "Summer Case Files" being delayed by almost a year has been torturous for those who care about it and equally so for LKY.

It torments LKY's spirit and body, as well as LKY's wallet.

An extra year has added a significant burden, nearly becoming the last straw that breaks the camel's back.

But having come this far, ending up in such a situation, just like LKY described "Summer Case Files" during crowdfunding, it's something LKY caused and must bear alone.

LKY has some minor strengths but also significant flaws. This flaw led LKY from favorable circumstances into adversity, even dire straits.

Overestimating one's capabilities while underestimating the complexity of each work process. Constantly making plans that are unachievable, feeling anxious and distressed as deadlines loom, paying the price over and over again, turning a good hand into a mess.

From owning a car, a house, savings, a wife, and children, LKY has become someone who only orders cheap takeout meals, not even planning to return home for the New Year.

"Summer Case Files" represents a new beginning for LKY, a form of atonement.

LKY has poured years of debt and guilt into this game.

But in truth, it's also extremely selfish, because LKY believes that "the purpose of an apology is to make oneself feel better. It does nothing to mend the harm caused."

Yet there's no other way but to apologize first and then find a way to make amends.

To express the desire to apologize through the game and then compensate with future efforts.

Regarding this delay:

This delay has little to do with the progress of the game, although significant updates have been made recently.

LKY removed potentially risky content from the game, especially content that might violate STEAM guidelines.

Since "Summer Case Files" is a visual novel set in high school times, it includes some cooler scenes and ambiguous plots. In this adjustment, LKY made modifications to avoid all these risks.

Also, "Summer Case Files" is a game that has already passed review, so there's no issue with getting stuck in the review process.

However, LKY is very timid, fearing that the game would be banned after launch due to violations, so adjustments were made and completed smoothly.

This delay mainly concerns ongoing promotional work.

After ten days of promotion, the wish list for "Summer Case Files" saw a noticeable increase, matching the number of wishes accumulated over the past six months within just ten days.

LKY feels extremely regretful and frustrated; if this promotional approach had started two months earlier, the situation would be entirely different.

But given the current state, LKY can only try to remedy the situation. LKY contacted some friends, hoping to conduct another round of promotions, aiming to increase the number of wish lists and market presence.

However, it's impossible to skip the Chinese New Year.

Therefore, LKY will delay "Summer Case Files" by another week, releasing it on either January 22nd or January 24th.

This request may seem unreasonable, but for the current LKY, everything must be done to ensure the game's successful release.

A week doesn't mean much for games with excellent promotional strategies, but for "Summer Case Files," it's crucial. The foundation of "Summer Case Files" is too weak; an additional week could nearly double the wish list.

LKY can feel everyone's concern and support.

With gratitude in heart but ashamed to accept it, LKY has consistently failed to live up to everyone's care and support until now.

But LKY can only express deep remorse here and hopes that you, watching on your screen, will allow LKY to release "Summer Case Files" without regrets.

PS: During the Spring Festival, "Summer Case Files" will remain operational, addressing any bugs and providing support after the game goes live.

notes.title: Summer Fantasy officially launches on January 15, 2025.
notes.notes:
Dear Supporters,
I am reaching out to you with a heavy heart and a sincere plea for understanding. We had initially planned to launch "Summer Incident Records" on January 3, 2025. However, due to unforeseen circumstances, we must now postpone the release until January 15th of this month. I sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.
As the primary person responsible for all aspects of "Summer Incident Records" apart from programming, I have been unable to focus on promotional activities until now because of the ongoing development work. Seeing the low number of wish list entries on our Steam page has been disheartening.
The original plan was to provide an early release as a token of appreciation to those who have supported me throughout the development process. Yet, after many sleepless nights considering the upcoming release, I have decided to make another announcement in hopes of gaining your understanding and support once more.
Over the past ten days, we've initiated some promotional efforts which have shown promising results. This success has reignited my hope that there is still much more we can achieve through further marketing. Due to personal limitations in time and resources, these efforts have been limited. However, even small steps have proven effective, and I would like to ask for your permission to dedicate the next two weeks to intensifying our promotional campaign.
A sufficient number of wish list entries on Steam are crucial for the successful launch of our game. Although two weeks is a short period, it represents one last effort to ensure we do not leave any stone unturned.
If you are passing by and reading this, I kindly ask for your support by adding "Summer Incident Records" to your Steam wish list. Your gesture would be greatly appreciated.
Thank you for your continued support and understanding.
Warmest regards, LKY and the "Summer Incident Records" Team

notes.title: Announcement of Extension (Kneeling) of Summer Event Book
notes.notes:
There is no justifiable reason, the Summer Event Book has been skipped.
LKY is very ashamed and pleads for another chance to polish the Summer Event Book better.
I was wrong! Sorry!
LKY's script changes too frequently, causing all colleagues in each stage to be exhausted and exhausted. The script has already been completed, but every time LKY reread the script, he couldn't help but make some changes. If we don't make any changes, we won't be able to sleep at night. LKY swears that this is the last time we will update the script.
The changes to the script have been completed now, and the work of adjusting the script is still ongoing. It is expected to be completed within a week.
LKY will submit the final version to STEAM for review during Labor Day. LKY is a newcomer in the AVG field and has also released a game on the STEAM platform for the first time. This release has consulted many professionals in the industry and received a lot of help. We would like to express our sincere gratitude.
In 2024, STEAM will be more and more strict in the review of anime products. LKY has carried out a comprehensive inspection of the game content and made some optimization to ensure that the platform can pass the review smoothly.
But as a newcomer, LKY is worried that his blind optimism will once again disappoint everyone.
During this period, LKY still has to contact publicity related work, which is a significant challenge for LKY who does everything except programming. For this reason, we hope to be cautious and allow LKY to submit for review first. Once the platform has approved the review, LKY will then announce the specific release date.
But even if there are some unexpected circumstances, the release date will not be postponed beyond May. Please give LKY another chance, thank you!
Once STEAM's review is approved, LKY will immediately notify everyone and announce the release date.
Thank you to every screen, thank you.

notes.title: The trial will start soon, thank you very much for coming!
notes.notes:
It is expected to open the DEMO version download before December 27, and I hope that each partner will give more opinions in the continuous improvement iteration.

This is a domestic Galgame about love and kindness.

We will keep our distance and restraint, and will sing softly at the exit of the subway like a wandering singer.

People in a hurry don't stop for life, but this song will not stop, it will be there today, and it will be tomorrow. I don't know how many times I passed by, one day you had dinner alone, and you hummed a light tune in your mouth while opening the takeout. Suddenly, I realized that this... Isn't that exactly the song that the wandering singer has been singing?

I would like to express my sincerest thanks to everyone in front of the screen and wish you good luck.
